x: It's a small world alright, particularly for Chris it seems, for when he was told that Frenchman Guy Monnet had joined us he remarked "That was the guy I accidentally tripped up in a cross-country race here in Canada a few months back".

After the first lap of the common it was Trevor Hart in the 'drivers seat' with a neat bunch of about 8 gathered around him including a bronzed Bob Smith, recently back from Australia and the most recent addition to our ranks Guy Monnet who hails from France.

Colin Pearson leads narrowly from John Thresher and Jim Rimmer with Guy Monnet, Laurie O'Hara, Mark McNair and John Keily following up in the Club 1500m championship.
The real bombshell was dropped by our French member Guy Monnet. Guy's 22nd place (fifth Bel) surprised most people, if not TomnCarter, and could not have come at a more opportune time.

Guy Monnet again showed up well, in fifth place, but John Kelly's 11th place in 46m. 6s. measured up best against Bill Lucas' yardstick, while veteran Charlie Manning pipped Guy for the third handicap spot.

It could be, at the same time, that Guy Monnet will produce an even more considerable breakthrough in coming weeks than he has already this winter, while Colin Pearson, John Kelly and Bob James are all threatening to break out of the second team ranks into the first team before long.

Even with a great breakthrough by Guy Monnet, who finished a magnificent 14th in 41m. 57s., we were still kept out of first place in the Surrey Cross-Country Championship, over 7-miles of fog-bound Wimbledon Common.
Guy Monnet again produced some good form to win at Ruislip over a supposed 7-miles in 42m. 08s., but had very little support.
Lionel Mann won his fifth official club championship of 1970-71 when he added the 10-mile title to his bag after a hard struggle with surprise packet Guy Monnet.

Trevor Hart must have been disappointed with 123rd, but not as disappointed as Guy Monnet - the most sharply improved runner in the club - who could have expected to finish at least 100 places higher than his 151st.
This race was held the same day as the National, and produced a win for Guy Monnet, who ranks with the "A" team these days, but was not eligible for Norwich.

Trials sometimes do something to sort out selection problems, but on this occasion the most important performance was put up by Guy Monnet, whose 15m. 06s. - slightly faster than the times returned by Tony Fairclough and Tony Binda - must have caused some headaches.
Good substitutes will be TONY FAIRCLOUGH, the galloping gourmets LIONEL MANN and GUY MONNET as well as TREVOR HART, JOHN BICOURT, LAURIE O'HARA, TONY BRIEN and ADRIAN MAJOR.

Chris Keavey took second place, off 560 yards, while Guy Monnet raced through to third place, off 220. There was a good run from Alan Black, but the fastest moving man in the field was 17-year old Peter Carton, who clocked 9m. 31s. off 120.
With a lap to go, we were in the hunt, but couldn't quite make it, in spite of good running by Guy Monnet, Charlie, and new member Bob Ker, who looks highly promising.

Jim Rimmer had a good win in the 800m. in 1m. 58.9s., and Guy Monnet took the 3,000m. in 8m. 50.4s., while Philip Gee gave our quarter-miling strength a boost when he won the 400m. in a personal best time of 51.0s.

Third place went to Guy Monnet, who also clocked the third fastest scratch time. Fastest man round the course was Trevor Hart, with 14m. 50s., while Alan Black chalked up the next best, with 15m. 03s.
This five-miler against Walton served as a farewell appearance for our popular French member, Guy Monnet - coming a few days before Guy was due to leave for a one-year stay in his native country.
